title: Oct. 24: Fort Tejon Paranormal Investigation with Marie Mason
excerpt: Join Ghost Hunter Marie Mason and her professional paranormal team and investigate Fort Tejon State Historic Park, a location with decades of documented activity, unsettling encounters and unexplained phenomena
content:
Join Ghost Hunter Marie Mason and her professional paranormal team and investigate Fort Tejon State Historic Park, a location with decades of documented activity, unsettling encounters and unexplained phenomena.

The Fort Tejon Paranormal Investigation in Lebec will be held on Saturday, Oct. 24, (a week before Halloween), 6-11:30 p.m.

This guided investigation will be held across historic sites like the 2-story Officer’s House, barracks, hospital ruins and the haunted oak tree using SLS cameras, Spirit Boxes and REM Pods, plus psychic readings.

Cost: Adults $50–$75, children under 12 $25.

Fort Tejon State Historic Park is a former U.S. Army frontier fort on the main route between the Central Valley and Southern California was garrisoned from 1854 to 1864.

Investigate at night with real ghost hunters including Marie Mason as seen on Discovery Channel’s “Ghost Adventures” on Dec. 31, 2025 “Pioche Episode.” Mason is the author of “Ghosts of Randsburg.”

Mason, a professional Ghost Hunter and her team will escort you through the park at night in a paranormal Investigation focusing on paranormally active locations that after five years of research have always produced paranormal activities.

You can talk to the people of the past, come document your own paranromal evidence.

Come early, have some food, and tell some campfire stories. The park will be open from 6-11:30 p.m.

“We will be investigating in allotted areas in time slots so groups are not over crowded. After or before your schedule time slot, you can sit by fire have food, tell stories, or investigate other areas such as the jail, guard shack, or the oak tree,” said Mason.

Be a part of a real Paranormal Investigation:

This is not a ghost tour.

This is not theater.

This is not a walking history talk.

New for this year:

The Officer’s House will be open, two story house (behind the plexi glass with guides).

Haunted Oak Tree (The legendary burial site of Lebec and the bear).

Food will include pulled pork served by the fire pit on the park grounds provided by Cindy from Randsburg Brown Sugar Sweets (food and desserts).

You will investigate active locations with guided groups:

— Officers’ two story house, behind the plexiglass, is a preserved colonial-style residence frozen in time.

— Barracks with Army uniforms, rifles, hats, beds and hospital artifacts, loaded with trigger items and past SLS activity.

— Quartermaster/Carpenter’s Tool Area with artifacts that remain in their original positions. Some areas viewed behind protective barriers.

— Blacksmith Building. Last year: iron tools moved live and SLS figures appeared working the fire pit.

— Haunted forest and wells with the old wells once used by the bakery and hospital. Known as a spirit gateway.

— The Oak Tree is a new location featuring an historic burial site tied to a chilling local legend.

Additional areas include:

— Guard House / Jail

— Orderlies’ Quarters

— Commissary / Hospital Ruins

— Cemetery Monument

— Grounds where buildings no longer stand.

The tour will provide top-of-the-line equipment, including:

— SLS Kinect Cameras

— SB7 Spirit Boxes

— DNA Alice Boxes

— Estes Method (headset)

— REM Pods & more

Bring your own equipment if you have it.

Small groups only with intimate, quiet and serious investigations.

Psychic readings by Ginny.

Your ticket allows after-hours access to the park where you can:

— Explore the grounds

— Sit by the fire pit (if open)

— Eat, relax, and share stories

Paranormal investigations are conducted during your assigned time slot.

Guided Tours will last 90-2hours

— Rangers on duty at all times

— Dress warm — it gets cold

— Bring flashlights

— Stay on dirt trails (gopher holes present)

Guided tours will be running every 90 minutes so choose your time when you purchase tickets: 7 p.m. 8:30 p.m. and 10 p.m.

If you want to buy equipment contact Marie Mason, she will bring extra to sell as she makes the tools.

— No live streaming during investigations

— Phone video is allowed

— No alcohol

— Respect park rules and rangers

— Children are allowed but use discretion—this is real and intense

Fort Tejon State Historic Park

Grapevine Canyon, Tejon Pass

Established August 10, 1854

Abandoned September 11, 1864

A site once occupied by:

— Native Americans

— Settlers & gold miners

— U.S. Army (pre-Civil War)
